beats: A full tanker is safe. An empty one too. Half full is the problem.
When the driver brakes, the truck slows down, but the liquid inside keeps going.
It rushes forward as one heavy wave and slams into the front wall.
That hit shoves the whole truck forward, even with the brakes on.
Then the wave bounces back, hits the rear wall, and returns. The truck rocks.
On an icy road, that wave can push a stopped tanker out into an intersection.
Full, the liquid has no room to move. Empty, there's nothing to push. Half full, it's a battering ram.
That's why most tankers hide walls inside, called baffles.
Each baffle is full of holes. Liquid still gets through, but only slowly.
The big wave is chopped into small ones, and each wall takes its own little hit.
So the danger isn't the weight. It's weight that keeps moving after you stop.
